title: Tiny Edge SDK — field notes & developer playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working notebook for a tiny-footprint SDK that teams can drop into edge devices (IoT gateways, ARM single-board computers, mobile background services) to call Redwood inference with predictable cost and safe offline behavior. Not a final spec — more of a field playbook with quickstart steps, sample flows, known constraints, and troubleshooting notes.

Audience:
- SDK devs building tiny clients
- Solutions engineers prototyping for customers with intermittent connectivity or strict memory/cpu budgets
- PMs evaluating tradeoffs for a lightweight offering

Goals (MVP):
1) <10MB runtime binary + deps (strip optional features)
2) Controlled token/bandwidth usage via local sampling + batching
3) Robust offline mode: enqueue + persistent queue, backoff retry, optimistic local responses for UX
4) Telemetry that is opt-in and privacy-friendly (local aggregation, sample percent)

Quickstart (5–10 min prototype):
1) Install prebuilt: pip install redwood-edge-sdk==0.1.0-prerelease or use wheel for armv7/arm64.
2) Add minimal config JSON (see example below) with api_key, region, device_id, offline_queue_path.
3) Call client.generate_short(prompt, max_tokens=64, mode=streamed) with local_cache=true.
4) Validate fallback: toggle airplane mode and confirm the request is queued and later delivered intact.

Minimal config example (plain text):
{
  "api_key": "<REDACTED>",
  "region": "us-west-2",
  "device_id": "gateway-42",
  "offline_queue_path": "/var/lib/rwd/queue.db",
  "telemetry": {"enabled": false, "sample_pct": 0.01}
}

Behavior notes / heuristics:
- Memory: keep in-memory buffers < 4MB. Use incremental chunked upload for queued items.
- Batching: local batched sends up to 8 small prompts or 1 long prompt. Prefer size-based batching (bytes) rather than count.
- Caching: prefix-KV cache for repeated prompts (session-level). Provide a TTL and size cap.
- Network: exponential backoff with jitter, max 6 retries, persist enough metadata to avoid duplication.
- Local fallback: for chat UX, show last good bot response + optimistic placeholder while queued request is pending.

Telemetry & privacy checklist:
- Default telemetry OFF. Must be explicit in onboarding.
- Aggregate locally: only send summaries (token counts, latency percentiles) not raw prompts.
- PII: detect and redact obvious PII before any external telemetry.
- Compliance: add KMS hint for enterprise customers who want telemetry encrypted in transit.

Developer ergonomics plan (short-term):
- Provide tiny CLI: rwd-edge init -> creates config, prompts for telemetry opt-in, creates a sample app.
- Offer CI smoke test: a small script that runs on-device emulator or QEMU to exercise network failure scenarios.
- Dev-friendly logs: two levels (dev/production), with prod logs obfuscating prompts.

Runbook: on first customer report of weird queued behavior
1) Ask for device logs (log level dev) and queue.db snapshot.
2) Check queue integrity tool (rwd-edge inspect-queue) to list pending items and checksums.
3) If duplication: compare item checksums, clear duplicates using tool with safe mode.
4) If persistent failures: capture pcap around retries, escalate to infra with ticket EDGE-412.

Open questions / TODOs (scratch):
- Should SDK expose a user-facing usage counter (tokens/day) or keep this server-side? pros/cons for offline billing.
- Compression: enable zstd for queued items? benchmark impact on CPU (esp. ARM Cortex-A7).
- Where to draw line between tiny SDK and full-featured client (e.g., function-calling)? propose feature flags.

Customer vignette idea (internal demo):
- Use case: logistics partner with 300 offline devices that sync overnight. Show worst-case cost with naive retry vs. batched sync + prefix caching.
- Metric to show: cost per successful message, median sync latency, and data transmitted per device per day.

Notes-to-self style reminders:
- Keep onboarding friction < 3 steps for initial test.
- Record short video of the CLI init flow (30–60s).
- Add unit test harness for intermittent network toggles (toggle network interface in VM).

Links & references:
- Internal: linear/EDGE-412, github/edge-sdk PRs (see header linked_artifacts)
- Benchmark idea: run 5 device classes (rpi-zero, rpi-4, jetson-nano, arm64 cloud emu, android background) and capture CPU/memory and energy.

End of notebook — very rough. Will split into a formal quickstart + README + tiny-cli next sprint.
